call_summary: A consultant pitched an AI lead-response 'employee' to the owner of a Houston roofing company. The call opened with a clear agenda and some useful discovery about the owner's manual intake process (office manager calling leads back, no standard follow-up, ~80 leads/month). The consultant prematurely linked the findings to the solution before quantifying the business impact, then introduced price ($3,000 setup, 14-day timeline). The owner raised trust objections rooted in a prior failed automation integration and demanded proof the product works with JobNimbus. The consultant declined to share client proof and ended with a vague email follow-up, leaving the buyer's stated criterion unresolved.

corrections.action: Before introducing the solution, quantify the cost of the problem with one impact question that converts the gap into lost revenue.
corrections.why: Anchoring the pain in dollars makes the price feel like an investment rather than a cost and gives the owner a reason to want the solution.
corrections.example_line: Of those eighty leads a month, if half wait over an hour, how many would you guess end up hiring another roofer before you reach them?

corrections.action: When a prospect names a specific tool, acknowledge it by name and ask about their integration history on that platform before claiming compatibility.
corrections.why: Specificity signals competence and surfaces the real risk (prior failed integration) early enough to address it with proof rather than a slogan.
corrections.example_line: Got it, JobNimbus. Have you tried connecting anything else to it before, or would this be your first automation on that platform?

corrections.action: Replace open-ended email promises with a specific, time-bound deliverable plus a calendar hold tied to the buyer's stated buying criterion.
corrections.why: A concrete next step with a deadline converts a soft maybe into a measurable commitment and keeps the deal from drifting into silence.
corrections.example_line: I will send you a JobNimbus-specific example by Thursday noon, and let's block fifteen minutes on Friday to walk through it together, fair?

recovery_line.text: Before I send anything, help me bring the right proof: what specifically would you need to see working inside JobNimbus to feel confident moving forward?
recovery_line.why: It converts an open-ended email promise into a buyer-defined success criterion, reopens diagnosis, and gives the next touch a concrete purpose the owner has agreed to.

replay_plan.opening_question: Before I show you anything, could you walk me through what happens today from the moment a new lead comes in until someone actually reaches them?
replay_plan.diagnostic_follow_up: Of the roughly eighty leads a month you get, how many do you estimate you lose to a competitor because they weren't called fast enough?
replay_plan.objection_clarifier: When you say the last automation company never finished, what specifically did they fail to deliver? That tells me exactly what I need to prove.
replay_plan.next_step_line: I will bring a JobNimbus-specific example by Thursday noon and we will put fifteen minutes on the calendar Friday to review it together, sound good?
